editorial:
If you want a cozy holiday comedy with kid-friendly chaos, this one delivers a familiar but fun ride. Ten-year-old Finn is not thrilled about leaving sunny California for a creepy old house in Maine, and his fear of ghosts turns into a full trap-building mission. When his parents get stuck across town, Finn and his sister are left to handle a group of thieves who want something hidden in the house. The vibe is light, silly, and easy to watch with the whole family.

The traps are the main draw, with plenty of slapstick moments and quick pacing that keeps things moving. The acting is cheerful, though the story feels very familiar if you have seen earlier Home Alone movies. It is best for younger viewers and anyone wanting background holiday fun. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for a movie night.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Finn’s traps stop the thieves one by one as they try to search the house. His sister helps, and the police arrive before the crooks can escape with the hidden painting. The parents finally make it home, the family is safe, and the holiday mood returns. The thieves are arrested, and Finn learns the house is not haunted after all.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family holiday comedies and silly trap-filled adventures.
similarMovies: Home Alone 2: Lost in New York
